description: A four-channel 64-step sequencer whose notes are written in from a CV input. Each channel has its own step position and its own length, and a fifth channel stages a sequence

params.text: Shows the CV display as volts, as note names using sharps, or as note names using flats
When on, the voltage at CV IN is rounded to the nearest semitone as it is written. It acts on what is written, so some channels can hold quantized notes and others not
Cycles the gate of the current step: a normal gate that follows the clock pulse width, a held gate that stays high for the whole step and ties into the next, or off
Steps on to the next channel for display and editing, through the four playing channels and the staging channel
Copies the pitches, gates and length of the selected channel. Pressing it again cancels a paste that is waiting
Pastes the copied channel into the selected channel, at the moment chosen by the PASTE SYNC switch
Starts and stops the sequencer. While it runs, the four playing channels follow their clocks and the staging channel does not
Stores the voltage at CV IN into the current step of the selected channel
Moves the selected channel one step to the left
Which voltage the selected channel's CV output carries while the sequencer is stopped: in the SEQ position the voltage stored at that step, in the other the voltage at CV IN
Moves the selected channel one step to the right
The number of steps the selected channel plays before repeating, 1 to 64. Each channel holds its own length, so sequences of different lengths can run together
Moves through the steps of the selected channel so they can be shown and edited
When on, a write advances the selected channel one step to the right
Returns every channel to its first step
Whether a paste happens at once, on the next clock, or at the start of the next sequence. A paste into the staging channel always happens at once, whatever this is set to

inputs.text: The voltage written into the current step; anything from -10V to 10V is stored
Sets or clears the gate of the step being written; with nothing patched, the stored gate is left as it was
A rising edge above 1V stores the voltage at CV IN into the current step
A rising edge above 1V moves the selected channel one step to the left
A rising edge above 1V moves the selected channel one step to the right
Advances channels 1 and 2 one step on each rising edge
Advances channels 3 and 4 one step on each rising edge; with nothing patched here, those two channels follow the clock at CLOCK 1,2
A rising edge above 1V returns every channel to its first step
A rising edge above 1V starts or stops the sequencer

outputs.text: The voltage stored at the step channel 1 is playing, 1V per octave when notes are stored
The voltage stored at the step channel 2 is playing, 1V per octave when notes are stored
The voltage stored at the step channel 3 is playing, 1V per octave when notes are stored
The voltage stored at the step channel 4 is playing, 1V per octave when notes are stored
The gate of the step channel 1 is playing, 10V when high
The gate of the step channel 2 is playing, 10V when high
The gate of the step channel 3 is playing, 10V when high
The gate of the step channel 4 is playing, 10V when high

menu: Arrow controls — sets whether the left and right buttons Step the selected channel or Rotate its contents
Reset on run — returns the play head to the start every time the sequencer is started
Retrigger gates on reset — holds the gate outputs low for 1ms after a reset so a trigger-sensitive target fires again; the choices are No, Yes, and Only when Run cable is unconnected
Portable sequence — holds Copy sequence and Paste sequence, which move the selected channel between this module and other sequencers that support the format
